There is no clock. Three strikes end the run, and you can also finish it yourself.
The hall is a game stage and every person, clinic and app is made up. In real life, complain to the organisation first, then the National Privacy Commission.
Listen to the witness. Statements come one at a time: use Back and Next to move through them, or open "Statements so far" to jump to one.
There is no clock. The game lasts three cases.
On the false statement, press OBJECTION!, then pick the evidence card that proves it. It can be a document, a screenshot or a rights card.
Press a statement to hear more detail. It costs nothing, and a nervous witness may slip.
A wrong objection is a strike: either the statement was true, or the card does not prove it. A clean case earns a bonus.

Take case after case at the barangay hall. In each one, the witness makes statements and one of them is false. Press for detail, shout OBJECTION! and present the right evidence. Cases get harder, and the run ends on your third strike.

Welcome to the barangay hall. Three cases are waiting: a leaked record, a claim wrongly flagged by AI, and a chatbot that gave harmful advice. In each one, the witness makes statements, and one of them is false. Find it, shout OBJECTION! and present the right evidence. Three strikes adjourn the hearing, and you always finish.
Which card proves this statement is false? A wrong card is a strike.
In real life: write to the organisation’s Data Protection Officer first, keep your records, and if nothing changes, go to the National Privacy Commission.
{n} cards: documents, screenshots and rights cards. Read them while you listen.

Do you lean too trusting or too doubtful?
Rough read: short rounds give only a rough picture. Play 10 items for a steadier one.
Nice balance! You trust the real posts and doubt the fake ones. That is calibrated trust.
You lean doubtful. Many posts are true! Check first, then decide. Doubting everything is tiring.
You lean trusting. When a post sounds too good or too scary, pause and check before you believe it.

Thank you for helping! Did something break, or did you spot wrong info?

A person helped, which always works. A kiosk that fits you is faster and does not need a line.

Good work. Most visitors were served. Fixes that help many people go a long way.
Open to All! Everyone was served. You kept the kiosk open to all.
Remember: trust tools that work for everyone you love. Ask for the human option when technology leaves someone out, and tell the health center what did not work.
A good start. Several people left, and that is what happens when a service leaves people out. Try again.
